headline: TSMC employee data leaks; a stolen key trojanizes an AI extension
standfirst: TSMC confirmed a leak of employee data, and a trojanized AI coding extension was traced to a stolen access key. Neither story carries a CVE. Italy fined Meta, and the Pentagon renamed its AI office.
bodyMarkdown:
## Breaches

TSMC confirmed that personal employee data was leaked online, after a threat actor put 6.9GB of allegedly stolen information up for auction [[s1]]. The headline links the incident to a cloud provider; the excerpt names neither the provider nor the access path. Analysis: a third-party route would shift scrutiny away from TSMC's own perimeter, but the supplied text does not establish one.

Cursor traced the compromise of Anthropic's official Claude Code extension on its marketplace to an access key it had issued to Fireworks AI, which exposed the key; an attacker used it to copy data from a read-only resource [[s4]]. Analysis: the chain is the story — one vendor's exposed credential becoming another's distribution problem.

## Industry

Italy's data protection authority fined Meta €805 million over a Facebook for Android feature that suggests gallery photos and videos for posting, finding it default-on and that the app accessed photos, videos and metadata without explicit consent; a 60-day window followed [[s3]].

The Pentagon renamed its CDAO the "Super Intelligence Office," following an order to swap "artificial intelligence" for "super intelligence" in executive branch communications [[s2]]. Analysis: a messaging change with no operational security effect evident here.

selected.title: Italy Fines Meta €805 Million Over Facebook's Android Gallery Access Without Explicit Consent
selected.excerpt: Meta was fined €805 million in Italy yesterday over a Facebook for Android feature that suggests photos and videos from users' phone galleries for them to post. selected.title: Pentagon Renames CDAO ‘Super Intelligence Office’
selected.excerpt: The move follows President Trump’s order to replace “artificial intelligence” with “super intelligence” in executive branch communications. The post Pentagon Renames CDAO ‘Super Intelligence Office’ appeared first on SecurityWeek.
